technique.how: Ask the patient (and any witness) whether a sensation of a racing, pounding or fluttering heartbeat began in the seconds to minutes before losing consciousness. Distinguish this from palpitations noticed only after waking, and ask whether they were rapid/regular, irregular, or 'skipped beats'.
technique.prerequisites: Patient able to recall the prodrome; a witness account helps when amnesia is present.

interpretation.positive_finding: Palpitations immediately before syncope are a recognised predictor of cardiac (arrhythmic) syncope in the EGSYS derivation cohort and were the only historical predictor of a cardiac cause in patients without heart disease in Alboni 2001.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence does not exclude arrhythmic syncope; many arrhythmic events produce no perceived palpitations, particularly bradyarrhythmias.
interpretation.pitfalls: Sinus tachycardia during a vasovagal prodrome or panic can be reported as palpitations; recall bias is common after loss of consciousness.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: treat as possible arrhythmic syncope - obtain ECG, consider monitoring/admission rather than discharge as vasovagal. Negative: does not lower cardiac probability.

sources.citation: Albassam OT, Redelmeier RJ, Shadowitz S, Husain AM, Simel D, Etchells EE. Did This Patient Have Cardiac Syncope?: The Rational Clinical Examination Systematic Review. JAMA. 2019;321(24):2448-2457.
Del Rosso A, Ungar A, Maggi R, et al. Clinical predictors of cardiac syncope at initial evaluation in patients referred urgently to a general hospital: the EGSYS score. Heart. 2008;94(12):1620-1626.
Alboni P, Brignole M, Menozzi C, et al. Diagnostic value of history in patients with syncope with or without heart disease. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2001;37(7):1921-1928.
Thavendiranathan P, Bagai A, Khoo C, Dorian P, Choudhry NK. Does this patient with palpitations have a cardiac arrhythmia? JAMA. 2009;302(19):2135-2143.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative answer to downgrade a patient with structural heart disease, abnormal ECG, or exertional/supine syncope.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Palpitations followed by syncope in a patient with known heart disease, a family history of sudden death, or an abnormal ECG warrants monitored observation and cardiology input.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Self-reported prodrome; reproducibility not reported in the sources.

extraction_notes: No numeric LR/sens/spec visible in accessible text. The 2019 RCE abstract (PMID 31237649) reports no palpitation estimate and the article is not PMC open-access, so its evidence table could not be read; the EGSYS abstract (PMID 18519550) names 'palpitations before syncope' as a multivariable predictor of cardiac syncope but gives no univariate accuracy; Alboni 2001 abstract (PMID 11401133) states 'in the patients without heart disease, palpitation was the only significant predictor of a cardiac cause' without a number. Estimates therefore left empty; a verifier with journal access should extract the palpitations row from RCE 2019 Table (likely LR ~2-3) and from EGSYS Table 2. All PMIDs confirmed by fetch; EGSYS DOI not returned by fetch so left null.
